legal.headline: Karnataka High Court quashes case against MedPlus over short supply of one tablet costing ₹1.12
legal.hook: Karnataka High Court quashes case against MedPlus over short supply of one tablet costing ₹1.12
legal.summary: The Court observed that the alleged short supply of one tablet, coupled with the collection of ₹1.12, did not establish that the accused had sold the drug at a price exceeding the permissible ceiling price.
legal.contextNote: Bar & Bench reports that the Karnataka High Court dismissed a complaint against MedPlus alleging short supply of a single tablet priced at ₹1.12. The court held that the alleged deficit of one tablet, together with the collection of ₹1.12, does not satisfy the test for contravention of the Drug Prices Control Order, 1995 (DPCO) ceiling‑price provisions. No specific statutory section is cited; the decision rests on the factual insufficiency to prove a price‑over‑ceiling violation. No precedent directly on point is identified.

legal.contextNote: The Delhi High Court affirmed a labour court order that an employee’s age be determined from her EPIC (Election Commission) record rather than her Aadhaar UIDAI data. The judgment underscores that Aadhaar, while a valid identity proof under the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Services) Act, 2016, is not conclusive for demographic details like date of birth when a statutory or regulatory record (EPIC) exists. No specific statutory provision was cited beyond the labour court’s discretion under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. No precedent directly on point was referenced; the decision aligns with earlier High Court observations that Aadhaar is a supplemental document, not a primary source for personal particulars.
